protocol_checks.vulnerability_mechanism: Confirmed: through neethi-3.2.1, PolicyReference.normalize() calls getRemoteReferencedPolicy() on a registry miss; that method passes the caller-controlled URI to URL.openConnection() without scheme or destination-address restrictions and follows HttpURLConnection redirects, enabling SSRF via arbitrary protocols and forbidden destinations.
protocol_checks.atomic_bic: Confirmed ee7f26a25bdb0bff6cbc611731159ba6f6f16032: bounded reverse -S searches for openConnection and getRemoteReferencedPolicy both identify this 2007 commit as the first Git write of the vulnerable remote-fetch path.
protocol_checks.immediate_parent_absence: Confirmed: the sole parent 8baf24289b8a2976f7df94adac1d1470ec80be13 exists and its PolicyReference only performs registry lookup then throws; tree-scoped search finds no openConnection or remote-policy fetch. The primary field introducer_parent_absent=false correctly denotes that the Git parent itself is present.
protocol_checks.squash_member_decomposition: Confirmed: the BIC is a single-parent non-merge commit, not a squash aggregate. Its message identifies an applied AXIS2-2451 patch; the public JIRA attachments attribute PolicyReference.diff to Nencho Lupanov in May 2007 and contain the same unrestricted URL.openConnection sink, with no finer Git member to substitute for the BIC.
protocol_checks.affected_release_membership: Confirmed: ee7f26a25bdb0bff6cbc611731159ba6f6f16032 is an ancestor of neethi-3.2.1^{commit}=9daf936fd3e3369307e773a6a8e492a3b64bfb22, whose PolicyReference still performs the unrestricted fetch; none of the remediation commits is an ancestor of 3.2.1.
protocol_checks.fixed_release_membership: Confirmed: 696e2489d2054eea01ba644ce4202121dd4ed6ef, 196862e97da09de193e5c663b6246a1cc476ce41, and 26f81a6b860135d557fb161850fb6d47e247a52f are ordered ancestors of neethi-3.2.2^{commit}=2351df23093e1bd4b2d2c8f9630e95e929a5de4e; CVE.org remains PUBLISHED and both CVE.org and Apache identify versions before 3.2.2 as affected.
protocol_checks.direct_fix_or_unpatched: Correction required: 696e2489d2054eea01ba644ce4202121dd4ed6ef adds the http/https allowlist and 196862e97da09de193e5c663b6246a1cc476ce41 adds the named address-class filter, but redirects remain enabled after both. Because the primary expressly includes redirect following in the mechanism, the complete direct-fix boundary is 26f81a6b860135d557fb161850fb6d47e247a52f, which calls setInstanceFollowRedirects(false).
protocol_checks.bic_only_ai_attribution: Confirmed NOT_AI: the exact BIC is dated 2007, has human Apache author/committer Sanka Samaranayake, no AI/bot/co-author/generated trailers, and points to contemporaneous JIRA patches submitted by Nencho Lupanov. No later AI-marked refactor or fix is used to attribute the BIC.

findings: The vulnerability, atomic BIC, parent-tree absence of the vulnerable mechanism, affected/fixed release topology, and NOT_AI attribution are independently confirmed.

primary fix_sha=196862e97da09de193e5c663b6246a1cc476ce41 is only the address-filter stage and does not close the primary's stated redirect-following mechanism; 26f81a6b860135d557fb161850fb6d47e247a52f is the first commit at which all stated SSRF mechanisms are closed.
